rationale: Variant or dialectal spelling of ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲟⲣⲉ 'stronghold' (already in glossary). On this page lines 1-2 the word appears as ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲡⲉ while lines 13, 20, 26, 30 use ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲟⲣⲉ. Same referent (cosmic strongholds surrounding the cosmos), possibly a scribal slip ⲡ for ⲣ.
Lycopolitan ⲧⲁⲩ = ⲧⲟⲟⲩ 'mountain.' With demonstrative ⲡⲓ-. Used in line 6 of 'this mountain of darkness' — a cosmographic feature. Distinct from ⲧⲁⲩ 'thousand' or ⲡⲧⲁⲩ 'the four.'

Lycopolitan verb of upward conveyance; possibly cognate with ⲱⲣϩ̄/ⲉⲓⲱⲣϩ̄ 'lift, raise.' Used in line 23 of the strongholds being raised up out of the earth (then cast upward to the height). Confidence moderate.
Latin fossa via Greek φόσσα. Cosmographic term in the disciples' question (line 22): the foundation-trenches upon which the strongholds were established. Manichaean cosmographic vocabulary.

Lycopolitan reflex of Coptic ⲉⲓⲏϩ/ⲉⲓⲱϩ 'torch, lamp, brand' (Crum 76b). Used in line 8: 'no lamp of light becomes manifest' — the cosmographic image of the volcanic mountain region where light cannot penetrate.
Likely directional ⲉ- + a Greek-derived terminal noun ⲡⲧⲉⲗⲁⲏ (cf. τέλος/τελευτή). Cosmographic-temporal terminus. Confidence moderate.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲇⲱⲗⲡ̄/ⲧⲱⲗⲡ̄ 'cover, envelop, hide.' Line 9: the gushing darkness covers the heaven from the side of radiance.

Apparent Lycopolitan/scribal variant for ⲧⲡⲉ 'heaven' in line 26. The Father of Life sends the strongholds from ⲛⲡⲓⲡⲉ 'from the heaven' — semantically equivalent to standard ⲛ̄ⲧⲡⲉ. Could be orthographic or dialectal.

Manichaean cosmographic technical compound: ⲡⲙⲁⲩ 'water' + ⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ 'Error' (in glossary). The corrupting watery substance sent into the midst of the upper archons in the cosmic purification process. Capitalization preserves the personified cosmic sense.
